doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.6c01786.summary: Multiconfigurational calculations compare radical-bridged lanthanide dimers across the series, separating crystal-field anisotropy from exchange interactions. The analysis identifies dominant virtual electron-transfer contributions in the gadolinium analogue and describes how exchange varies despite a broadly similar crystal-field potential.
doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.6c01786.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Provides a molecular-level framework for interpreting radical-mediated exchange and anisotropy; this is a computational magnetism study, not a qubit-coherence demonstration.

relatedPapers.reason: Connects radical-based molecular architectures with the control of magnetic interactions.

doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.6c00858.archiveJournal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.6c00858.summary: A hierarchical reaction-coordinate transformation maps multistate harmonic environments into chains of collective modes. Benchmarks include spin-boson and molecular charge-transfer models; truncated chains reproduce the tested dynamics with fewer degrees of freedom while exposing relationships between nuclear motion and electronic populations.
doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.6c00858.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Offers a computational route for reducing structured environments in models of molecular spin and charge dynamics; accuracy must be checked for each truncation.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use explicit environment models to study dynamics beyond simple perturbative relaxation descriptions.
